theme.description:
The theme: a name ("Deepharness", "Omarchy", "One Dark", …), or one
per system appearance. Unset means Omarchy when installed, else
Deepharness.

ui_font_family.description:
The font of everything but terminals and code (".ZedSans" is IBM
Plex Sans, bundled).

ui_density.description: How tightly the UI is spaced.

command_line.description:
The command line above the status bar, always there. Off, it shows
only while it has the keyboard (`ctrl-;`).

daemon.description: ainetd itself: starting it, its log, its socket.

runtimes.description: How Claude Code, Codex and shells are started in seats.

permissions.description: Permission requests held for you, and `/always` rules.

default.message_note: (Answer with the ainet tool reply_message id={id} — or on the shell: ainet msg reply {id} "…". Do not answer in this chat; the sender cannot see it.)
default.mention_note: (Answer with the ainet tool chat_send, or read more with chat_read.)

watchdog.message: [ainet] watchdog wake: check your queue (queue_list mine=true / ainet queue list --mine) and carry on with what you own.

hooks.description: ainet's hooks in Claude Code's settings.

retention.description: What ainetd keeps, and for how long.

ThemeSelection.description: A theme by name, or one for light and one for dark, as in Zed.

oneOf.description: Follow the system's light or dark appearance.

UiDensity.description:
Specifies the density of the UI.
Note: This setting is still experimental. See [this tracking issue](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/18078)

oneOf.description: A denser UI with tighter spacing and smaller elements.
A looser UI with more spacing and larger elements.

font_size.description:
In pixels, 6 to 100. Unset, it follows the UI: 13 at the default
`ui_font_size` of 16, so terminals read like the text around them.

line_height.description: The height of a line, as a ratio to the font size.

cursor_shape.description: The cursor of a focused terminal.

LineHeight.description: A terminal's line height, written as in Zed's settings.

oneOf.description:
1.3: box-drawing characters join up, which agents' TUIs rely on;
so it is ainet's default, unlike Zed's.

CursorShape.description: The cursor of a focused terminal, with Zed's names.

Blinking.description:
Whether a focused terminal's cursor blinks, with Zed's names. ainetd
does not pass on a program's own blink request, so
`terminal_controlled` keeps the cursor still.

dock.description: Its side of the window; the Agent panel takes the other.

width.description: In pixels; Zed's default side-dock width.

size.description: Their size in the Fleet (`ctrl-e` toggles it).

autostart.description:
Start ainetd in the background when the console or the desktop app
needs it and it is not running. Off, they say so and you start it
yourself (`ainet daemon`).

socket.description:
The daemon's socket. `$AINET_SOCKET` wins; unset, it is
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ainet.sock`. After a daemon restart.

restore_rigs.description:
Start again the seats of rigs that were running when ainetd last
stopped. Off, they come back stopped and `ainet up <rig>` restores
them.

log.description: ainetd's log. After a daemon restart.

level.description:
What to log: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`, or a
tracing filter (`info,ainet_daemon=debug`). `$AINET_LOG` wins.

file.description:
Where an autostarted ainetd writes its log. Unset, it is
`ainetd.log` in ainet's state directory.

append.description: Add to the log instead of starting it afresh on each autostart.

max_size_mb.description:
Once the log is this many megabytes, it is moved aside
(`ainetd.log.1`, …) when ainetd next starts. 0 never rotates.

keep.description: How many rotated logs to keep.

readiness.description: When a new seat counts as ready for its first message.

binary.description:
The program: a name on `PATH` or a path. Unset, `claude` or
`codex`.

model.description: The model of seats whose spec names none.

effort.description: Reasoning effort of seats whose spec names none.

permission_mode.description:
Claude Code's permission mode for new seats. Unset, Claude Code's
own default. `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk` and
`bypassPermissions` let agents act without asking you;
`bypassPermissions` skips every permission check.

args.description: Further arguments for every seat of this runtime.

env.description: Further environment variables for every seat of this runtime.

allowed_tools.description:
Tools allowed without asking, beyond ainet's own (`mcp__ainet`).
Each one loosens safety: the agent no longer asks before using it.

disallowed_tools.description: Tools the agent may not use.

mcp_servers.description:
MCP servers given to every seat besides ainet's, by name, as
Claude Code's `mcpServers` entries.

strict_mcp_config.description: Only ainet's MCP server and `mcp_servers`, none of your own.

oneOf.description: Ask before anything risky (Claude Code's default).
Less safe: file edits without asking.
Less safe: Claude Code decides what needs asking.
Less safe: never ask; what would need asking is refused.
Unsafe: no permission checks at all.

args.description: Further arguments for every shell seat.

env.description: Further environment variables for every shell seat.

timeout_secs.description:
How long to wait for a new seat to be ready before typing its
startup texts anyway, in seconds.

trust_timeout_secs.description:
The same once Claude Code asks whether to trust the folder (you
answer that), in seconds.

poll_ms.description: How often the screen is checked, in milliseconds.

quiet_ms.description:
Quiet time after the last output before a seat counts as ready,
in milliseconds, per runtime.

startup_text_gap_ms.description: Pause between a seat's startup texts, in milliseconds.

hold_secs.description:
How long a permission request waits for you in the Inbox before
the agent's own terminal dialog takes over, in seconds.

persist_always.description:
Keep `/always` rules after a session ends and across daemon
restarts. Less safe: an answer given once keeps allowing.

sensitive_paths.description:
Paths `/always` never covers, on top of ainet's own list (`.ssh`,
`.git`, `.env`, …): names, or paths under your home.

spec_policies.description:
Apply a rig spec's `permission_policy` where Claude Code allows it.
Off, it is reported and ignored, as before.

paste_settle_ms.description:
Between pasting a message into a terminal and pressing Enter, in
milliseconds: the agent's input box needs a moment to take it.

flush_gap_ms.description:
Between held messages delivered one after another, in
milliseconds.

hold_while_interacting.description:
Hold messages while you are at an agent's terminal, and deliver
them when you leave it.

typing_guard.description:
New seats start with their typing guard on: messages are held
until it is turned off.

message_note.description:
The last line typed with a message, telling the agent how to
answer. `{id}` is the message's number.
message_note.default: (Answer with the ainet tool reply_message id={id} — or on the shell: ainet msg reply {id} "…". Do not answer in this chat; the sender cannot see it.)

mention_note.description: The last line typed with a chatroom mention.
mention_note.default: (Answer with the ainet tool chat_send, or read more with chat_read.)

nudge.description:
Tell a queue item's destination about it right away, unless the
request says otherwise (`--no-nudge`).

watchdog.description: Watchdogs: reminders typed into a seat every so often.

default.message: [ainet] watchdog wake: check your queue (queue_list mine=true / ainet queue list --mine) and carry on with what you own.

default_interval_secs.description: The interval of a watchdog registered without one, in seconds.

min_interval_secs.description: The shortest interval allowed, in seconds.

message.description: What a watchdog registered without a message types.
message.default: [ainet] watchdog wake: check your queue (queue_list mine=true / ainet queue list --mine) and carry on with what you own.

tick_secs.description:
How often due watchdogs and blocked items' wakes are checked, in
seconds.

spec_dirs.description:
More directories of your own specs, searched after
`~/.config/ainet/specs` (the first one with a name wins).

default_cwd.description:
Where a rig created from one seat, or a loose agent, runs when no
directory is given. Unset, the console's current directory, else
your home.

snapshot_on_down.description: `ainet down` takes a snapshot first unless told `--no-snapshot`.

keep_snapshots.description:
Keep only this many snapshots per rig, the newest; older ones are
deleted. Unset, every snapshot is kept.

claude_sessions.description:
Show every Claude Code session on this machine in the Fleet, from
`~/.claude/sessions`. Off, only agents ainet started or adopted,
and sessions that report through ainet's hooks.

tmux.description: Look for agents in tmux panes when asked to discover.

interval_ms.description: How often Claude Code's sessions are checked, in milliseconds.

transcripts_ms.description:
How often context use, model and last tool are read from
transcripts, in milliseconds.

claude_settings.description:
Claude Code's settings file that `ainet install-hooks` edits.
Unset, `settings.json` in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`.
Nothing is written there without you asking.

messages_in_memory.description: Messages ainetd keeps in memory (all stay on disk).

chat_in_memory.description: Chatroom posts ainetd keeps in memory (all stay on disk).

inbox_items.description: Inbox items kept; answered ones go first, waiting ones never.

scrollback_lines.description: Rows of scrollback each new terminal keeps.

events_max_age_days.description: Delete logged events older than this many days. Unset, kept.

events_max_count.description: Keep at most this many logged events, the newest. Unset, all.

inbox_expiry_mins.description:
Drop answered inbox items this many minutes old. Unset, they
stay until the inbox is full.

prices.description:
Prices by model-id prefix (`claude-opus-5`), over the built-in
table; the longest matching prefix wins.

context_windows.description:
Context windows in tokens by model-id prefix, over ainet's guess
(1M for a `[1m]` model, else 200k).
